This vignette covers the last mile of the preparation workflow: what
exactly to upload, how to package supplementary files, and what happens 
to your files once TRIA receives them.
It assumes you have already been through `vignette("workflow")` and have
a complete `QWAmetadata` object and `QWAdata` files (and, optionally, a
validated zip of supplementary files) ready on disk.

---

## What to submit

A submission consists of:

1. **The `QWAmetadata` `.json`**: exported from the Shiny metadata app
   (`<date>_TRIA_<ds_name>_collected_metadata.json`) or written with
   `write_QWAmetadata()`.
2. **`{dataset_name}_QWAcells.csv(.gz)`** and
   **`{dataset_name}_QWArings.csv(.gz)`**: written with
   `write_QWAdata()`. The rings file may also have been saved via the Shiny
   flags app, if it was used for assigning data quality flags to years.
3. Optionally, **one zip archive of supplementary files** (original
   and annotated images, raw ROXAS / ROXAS AI output, reference series,
   etc.) and the **supplementary CSV** describing it (see
   `vignette("supplementary")`).

To hand over these files, email [tria@wsl.ch](mailto:tria@wsl.ch) and either:

- share a link to them on a file transfer service of your choice (e.g.
  Dropbox, Google Drive, your institution's own service); or
- ask for an invite link to WSL's file transfer server, if you'd rather
  not set one up yourself.

---

## What happens after you submit

We run your data through some basic validation checks, then insert it
into the TRIA PostgreSQL database.
This is where the structured data (measurements, metadata) live, and
what the TRIA web platform (webapps.wsl.ch/tria) talks to. Access is
controlled, so only the publicly available (meta-)data is visible
via the website.

### S3 bucket
For every dataset, we store the TRIA dataset files (metadata, cells,
rings and any supplementary files) in an S3 bucket: public datasets in the
public bucket, where they are easily accessible and downloadable, and
embargoed ones in a restricted bucket until their release.
Each dataset gets its own folder like this:

```
tria.0000/
  data/
    tria.0000_QWAmetadata.json
    tria.0000_QWArings.csv.gz
    tria.0000_QWAcells.csv.gz
  supplementary/
    tria.0000_supplementary_files.csv 
    tria.0000_supplementary_data.zip
  versions/                            <- only if there are multiple versions of the dataset
    tria.0000_v1_QWAmetadata.json
    tria.0000_v1_QWAcells.csv.gz           
```

We make a small number of server-side adjustments to your raw files during
ingestion, so that what ends up in the TRIA S3 bucket differs slightly
from what you submitted. None of these require any action on your part,
they're listed here purely so the shape of the final record isn't a
surprise.

### `QWAcells.csv`

Derived cell measurements (`tca`, `rwd2`, `dcwt`, `cwtall_adj`, `cdrad`,
`cdtan`, `cdratio`, `sector100`) are **removed**. They are trivially
recomputed from the raw measurements, so we don't store a second,
potentially stale copy. Recompute them with `complete_QWAdata()`.

### `QWArings.csv`

Ring flags are stored as in the database: missing flag values become
`FALSE`, and optional quality flag and comment columns that are empty in
all rows are not written.

### `QWAmetadata.json`

| Field | Change | When |
|---|---|---|
| `$dataset$ds_access`, `embargoed_until` | Removed | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$ds_label`, `url` | Added | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$citation` | Added (with the DOI if registered, otherwise the TRIA web app URL) | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$dataset_version` | Added (for reproducibility in case of later changes) | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$doi` | Added | When a DOI is registered |
| `$dataset$ds_license` | `"All rights reserved"` while embargoed; the submitted licence applies on release | On ingestion / release |
| `$images$fname_image`, `fname_cells`, `fname_rings`, `fname_settings` | Removed | On ingestion |
| `$related` | Removed (shown on the TRIA web app landing page) | On ingestion |
| `$datafiles` | Added: two rows for the `QWAcells`/`QWArings` files | On ingestion |

The `fname_*` columns hold absolute paths from your own machine---
meaningful while you're preparing the data, meaningless (and potentially
revealing local file-system structure) once archived, so they are always
stripped rather than carried into the database.
`$datafiles` contains two rows describing the `QWAcells` and `QWArings`
files, with `size_bytes`, `checksum` (MD5) and `s3_key`, so the data
files of each `dataset_version` are identified exactly.
Note that the supplementary CSV is a separate file (see below), not a
component of `QWAmetadata.json`.

### `supplementary_files.csv` and `supplementary_data.zip`

Providing a submission manifest means naming problems (an unrecognised file, a
missing `linked_label`) surface on your end, where you can still rename
or annotate things, rather than during our ingestion checks. We re-run
`check_supplementary()` on our side regardless, pointed directly at your
uploaded zip. If you provide the manifest CSV, it's trusted as ground
truth for anything it lists that's still in the zip. Extra files in the 
zip the manifest doesn't mention are left out rather than guessed at;
`check_supplementary()` warns about them, so you can declare them in the
manifest or remove them from the zip.
If you don't provide a manifest, we build one from scratch the same way
`compile_supplementary()` would for you. But any issues with inferring the
resource types and linked labels would mean that we have to contact
you for clarification---prolonging the submission process.

The checked and 'cleaned' archive is re-zipped.
For the supplementary CSV, the columns `fname_resource`, `status` and
`note` are removed, and `size_bytes` and `checksum` are added to identify
each file within the archive.
